entries.claim: SEBI SIF (Specialized Investment Fund) category, effective 1 Apr 2026: Rs.10L minimum, long-short strategy categories, MF Lite sibling framework; PMS Rs.50L and AIF Rs.1Cr minimums unchanged
entries.notes: Minimum, breach rules, and cost caps were sourced from secondary guides summarizing the SEBI text. Confirm against SEBI circulars and scheme documents before advising.

entries.claim: SEBI FY26 retail F&O data: 78.6 lakh individual traders, net losses Rs 91,685 cr, avg loss Rs 1,16,654; 87.7% of traders lost; F&O STT collections Rs 27,695 cr (FY26)

Budget 2026 removed the capital-gains exemption on SGBs purchased from the secondary market (effective 1 Apr 2026); only original subscribers holding to maturity retain the tax-free redemption; no new SGB tranches in FY 2026-27

FY 2026-27 LRS TCS structure (Finance Act 2026, eff. 1 Apr 2026): loan-funded education 0%; self-funded education/medical 2% above Rs 10L; overseas tour packages 2% flat (no threshold); other LRS purposes 20% above Rs 10L; LRS limit USD 250,000/FY unchanged

IRDAI 2025-26 health-insurance reforms: PED waiting capped at 3 years; entry-age limit removed; moratorium period cut from 8 years to 5 (60 months, Feb 2026) - post-60-month repudiation only on proven fraud
DICGC deposit-insurance limit is ₹5 lakh per depositor, per bank, per same right & capacity (unchanged since the 2015 limit revision; joint accounts: ₹5L per joint holder)
FD rates Aug–Oct 2026: major banks 1-yr ~6.25–7.10% (SBI 6.25%, 444-day Amrit Vrishti 6.45%); small-finance banks up to 8.5% senior / 8.25% general; SFB per-depositor liability cap ₹25L
RBI phased weekly credit-bureau reporting: framework w.e.f. 1 Apr 2026, lenders to file borrower data 4×/month (9th/16th/23rd/last day) from 1 Jul 2026, replacing monthly/fortnightly cycles
ESOP/RSU two-stage taxation (Sec 17(2)(vi) perquisite at exercise + capital gain at sale) unchanged in the IT Act 2025; listed-equity CG FY 2026-27: LTCG 12.5% after 12 months, STCG 20%

Gifts > ₹50,000 in a year from a non-relative (or outside the Sec 57(xii) 'relative' list) are taxable to the recipient at slab rates; gifts from the specified relative list and on marriage are exempt

Unabsorbed capital losses carry forward 8 assessment years under Sec 70(3) only if the ITR for the loss year is filed by the Sec 139(1) due date; STCL is flexible (STCG+LTCG), LTCL is LTCG-only; speculation losses do not carry under 70(3)

Sec 87A rebate makes total tax zero when total taxable income ≤ ₹12 lakh (FY 2026-27 new regime; unchanged from the Budget 2025 reset) — harvesting a capital loss in a below-threshold year has no in-year value
Home-loan interest deduction under Sec 24(b): up to ₹2L p.a. for self-occupied property; new-regime slabs FY 2026-27 unchanged from the Budget 2025 reset
EPF interest rate 8.25% for FY 2025-26 (retained by CBT 239th meeting, Mar 2026; second consecutive year); EPF Scheme 2026 keeps 8.25%

IRDAI FY 2025-26: life death-claim settlement ~99%; ~1 in 12 (~8%) health claims rejected; 1-hour cashless pre-auth met in 86.8% of cases; avg health payout ~Rs 29,000; ICR public >100%, private 75-85%

SEBI+RBI cap the Indian MF industry's direct overseas equity at USD 7B (+ USD 1B global ETFs + USD 1B/AMC), set 2008, unraised; ceiling breached Jan 2022; as of 10 Jul 2026 only one domestic international fund open for fresh SIPs; GIFT City IFSCA funds are outside the cap

Non-government NPS exit: PFRDA 16 Dec 2025 amendment allows 80% lump sum / 20% min annuity (was 60/40), deferment to age 85, 100% withdrawal for corpus under Rs 8L; Section 10(12A) tax exemption still covers only 60% of the corpus

NPS deductions: 80CCD(1B) Rs 50,000 extra (old regime, incl. NPS Vatsalya from FY 2025-26); 80CCD(2) employer up to 14% both regimes (raised from 10% private, FY 2025-26); combined employer EPF+NPS+superannuation exempt cap Rs 7.5L/yr
ELSS: Rs 1.5L 80C (old regime only), 3-year lock-in per allotment; equity MF LTCG 12.5% above Rs 1.25L/yr shared bucket (Finance No.2 Act 2024); REIT/InvIT units share the same Sec 112A exemption

REPORTED (secondary): Budget 2026 raised 80TTB senior-citizen interest deduction to Rs 1L and doubled the TDS threshold; Income Tax Department threshold page still shows Rs 50,000 - verify before AY 2026-27 filing

HUF: separate taxable person (Sec 2(31)), own PAN, ITR-2/ITR-3; clubbing of member-gifted property income under Sec 64(2) of the 1961 Act = Sec 99(3)-(4) of the Income Tax Act 2025 (in force 1 Apr 2026); Vineeta Sharma partition is not taxable

REIT/InvIT: Sec 115UA pass-through; dividend exempt only if SPV NOT under 115BAA; 194LBA TDS 10% no threshold (resident); return-of-capital 56(2)(xii) from AY 2024-25; 112A LTCG 12.5% above Rs 1.25L, 111A STCG 20% under 12 months; TA Amendment Act 2026 (assent 17 Aug 2026) touched dividend wording - re-verify

Q2 2026 NCD bands: AAA 7.0-8.0%, AA 8.0-9.5%, A 9.5-11.5%, BBB 11.5-13%+; repo floor 5.25%, 10-yr G-Sec ~6.5-6.8%; NCD tax FY 2026-27: coupon at slab, no TDS (listed, resident demat), LTCG 12.5% no indexation; CRISIL 3-yr cohort defaults A 1.5-3%, BBB 3-5%

SIF: Rs.10L aggregate minimum at the PAN level (excludes AMC-mandated employee investments); accredited-investor exemption; framework effective 1 April 2026 - the first professional rung a Rs.10L reader is already eligible for

SEBI notified a revamped PMS regulation effective April 2027 introducing a mutual-fund-only PMS route at a Rs.25L minimum (below the classic Rs.50L PMS floor) - a new low-ticket pooled rung between SIF and classic PMS; re-verify the exact minimum and go-live date
AIF: Rs.1Cr minimum (Rs.25L for angel funds and manager-employee/director investors); Cat I/II close-ended with a 3-year minimum tenure; up to 1000 investors per scheme (49 angel)

Advance tax FY 2026-27: duty when tax after TDS exceeds Rs.10,000; cumulative 15/45/75/100% on 15 Jun / 15 Sep / 15 Dec / 15 Mar; 234C 1%/mo on each shortfall (3-month tails first three, 1-month last); 234B 1%/mo from 1 Apr when advance paid under 90% of assessed; capital-gains 31-Mar relief; 44AD/44ADA single 15-Mar payment
FY 2026-27 ITR standard deadline 31 July 2027 (non-audited), 15 July 2027 (audited); the exact dates are a published annual notification to re-verify at year-end

SIF strategy families (SEBI MF Regs 2026, secondary): seven permitted long-short / relative-value families; illustrative 75/25 blend with ~25% naked-short cap; ~2.25% management + ~2% distribution expense; daily NAV pricing; SIP/STP allowed
entries.notes: The "seven families" and the 75/25 blend are secondary-guide readings, not a fixed SEBI named list; verify the exact caps against the SEBI circular and each scheme document.

entries.claim: Finance Bill 2026 (assent 17 Aug 2026) makes the REIT/InvIT dividend component more uniformly exempt to unitholders regardless of the SPV regime, with a higher 25% SPV surcharge trade-off; interest / rental components stay slab-taxed; 115UA(2) current-year wording must be verified with a CA
entries.notes: The 25% SPV-surcharge figure and the dividend-uniformity mechanics are from the Lok Sabha 2026 amendment report; confirm against the final Finance Act text and the REIT/InvIT distribution statement.

entries.claim: SEBI AIF Amendment 2026: accredited-investor-only schemes waive the 1,000-investor cap; angel funds are a distinct Category I class (49-investor, accredited-only, re-registration deadline 8 Sep 2026); inoperative-fund classification and Regulation 29 retained-liquidation-proceeds changes; AIF Master Circular 3 Jun 2026
entries.notes: Secondary reading of the SEBI amendment; confirm deadlines and amendment numbers against the SEBI AIF Master Circular (3 Jun 2026).

entries.claim: AIF tax forms: 64C/64D migrate to 78/79 under the Income-tax Act 2025 (effective 1 Apr 2026, Sec 224 / Rule 145); income for years beginning before 1 Apr 2026 stays on the old forms; 194LBB 10% TDS on credited pass-through income; business income not passed through; losses need a 12-month hold
entries.notes: The 115UB pass-through and 194LBB TDS are current; the form renumbering is a 2026 framework change - re-verify at each Finance Act and against the Income-tax Department ITR-2 documentation.

entries.claim: Standard AIF GP-LP ladder: 2%/yr mgmt fee (committed capital in investment period, NAV/invested in harvest), 20% carry, 8% IRR hurdle, 100% catch-up; worked 3x/10-yr fund gives LP ~2.6x net, GP ~5-6% of fund value all-in; GP earns fee-only on a failure
entries.notes: Practitioner reading; verify the specific ladder against each fund PPM before advising.

entries.claim: 80CCD(1B) Rs 50,000 extra NPS deduction is OLD-REGIME-only (disallowed under new regime Sec 115BAC); only 80CCD(2) employer NPS (14% of Basic+DA for all employers, raised from 10% private-sector by Budget 2024) survives in the new regime. A blog intro claimed 80CCD(1B) is 'available even under the New Regime', but the same site's CA-reviewed body (15 Oct 2026) and FAQ table state old-regime-only - consistent with existing src-nps-deductions-2026
entries.notes: Conflicting claims found during Wave 8 research (ELSS/NPS tax-shield planning). Resolution: old-regime-only, per the CA-reviewed 15 Oct 2026 review plus 1 Finance/ClearTax coverage. Re-verify at each Finance Act; Wave 9 ELSS/NPS tax-shield calculators must use 80CCD(1B) old-regime-only.

entries.claim: PPF interest rate 7.1% p.a. for FY 2026-27 Q1 (unchanged, 8th straight quarter); re-notified quarterly

entries.claim: Modeled FY 2026-27 result: with the Budget 2025-widened new-regime slabs + 87A to 12L + 75k standard deduction, the NEW regime is cheaper than the old regime up to ~45L of income even with a full ~5L old-regime stack (80C 1.5L + 80CCD(1B) 0.5L + 24(b) 2L + 80D 1L); the old regime can only win with larger relative deductions (heavy 80D + 80E + top bands with surcharge). Verified by the deductionShieldFY27() unit-test scan.
entries.notes: Model excludes surcharge + 4% cess above 50L - the regime flip for >50L earners must be re-checked including surcharge. Re-verify at each Finance Act because any new-regime slab change flips the boundary.

entries.claim: Unlisted shares: 24-month LTCG holding period (unchanged by Budget 2024; the 36-month period was removed for most other assets), long-term gain taxed at slab rates without indexation; listed equity-type (shares, equity MF, business-trust units) is 12-month LTCG at 12.5% above the shared Rs 1.25L 112A pool
entries.notes: Verified against the PIB Budget-2024 FAQ and the Finance Bill 2024 memo (holding periods: 12-month listed, 24-month unlisted/property/gold, 36-month removed). This is the rate the AIF Cat I/II pass-through wedge in the tax-wedge article uses at the investor slab.

entries.claim: Category III AIFs are taxed at the fund level, frequently at the maximum marginal rate ~42.7% including surcharge; unitholders receive distributions net of that tax; specific vehicles may qualify for 10(4D)/10(23FF)/10(23FBC)/115AD exemptions
entries.notes: Secondary reading (Altportfunds / Treelife 2026); confirm the specific fund tax note and the exact current-year rate before advising on a Cat III sleeve.

entries.claim: FY 2026-27 individual surcharge: new regime 10%/15%/25% capped above 2Cr (the 37% top rate abolished for the new regime under the Income-tax Act, 2025, effective 1 Apr 2026); old regime keeps 37% above 5Cr; 15% surcharge cap on listed-equity 111A/112A tax; 4% HEC on (tax + surcharge after marginal relief)
entries.notes: Income-tax Act, 2025 (assent 21 Aug 2025) position per CA-published secondary source; re-verify the bands at each Finance Act and against the Income-tax Department threshold tables. The highIncomeTaxFY27() function models these bands.

entries.claim: Sec 56(2) gifts: relative gifts exempt with no limit; non-relative gifts aggregate over Rs 50,000 in a year makes the entire amount taxable at slab (a cliff); wedding/inheritance/12A-trust gifts always exempt; Budget 2025 did not change the threshold
entries.notes: The 50k cliff and the relative-list are stable; re-verify at each Finance Act.

entries.claim: Sec 64(2) self-acquired-to-HUF clubbing is renumbered Sec 99(3)-(4) in the Income-tax Act, 2025 (effective 1 Apr 2026); Sec 64(1)(iv) spouse-income and 64(1A) minor-income carry through; Sec 65 joint-and-several liability of the transferee remains
entries.notes: Confirm the exact Act-2025 section numbers against the Income-tax Act, 2025 text before advising a HUF structure; the AIS cross-PAN matching makes the clubbing triggers leave an electronic audit trail.
